title: updates.v2
description: Update availability, as computed on the site. v1 with one addition: a plugin may carry the release notes for the versions between the one it is running and the one it could run. Still an allowlist — anything absent is rejected, not ignored, and there is still no download URL and no licence key. The notes are the text a plugin already publishes to the Craft Plugin Store, and the site already holds them; forwarding them saves the platform from having to ask a third party what every plugin in a fleet is called. What makes that safe is what the receiver does with them: notes are stored against a plugin and a version, never against a site, so a database learns 'this version fixed that' rather than 'that site is exposed to this'. A receiver that stores them per site has reintroduced exactly the problem v1 refused, and no schema can stop it.

checked_at.description: Unix timestamp of the check itself, which may be well before the report is sent.

security_release_available.description: Whether any release between current and latest is flagged critical. This is the field that decides whether a site is urgent.

abandoned.description: Composer's abandoned flag. Worth surfacing: an abandoned plugin will never receive a security fix.

releases.description: The versions between current and latest, newest first. Sent only for a plugin that has an update available — there is nothing to describe otherwise. These bounds are an outer limit rather than a budget: a sender is expected to stop well short of them, because 250 plugins each carrying ten full release notes is a request nobody wants to receive.

notes.description: The release note as the plugin published it, in Markdown. Untrusted third-party text: a receiver renders it with HTML stripped or not at all.

date.description: Release date as the plugin store gave it. A string rather than a date, because it is displayed and never compared.

php.description: Whether the runtime itself is still supported. Counts and versions only.
